newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss KOF barometer up 0.1 pct in Nov vs Oct.
newsitem.headline: Swiss KOF barometer up 0.1 pct in Nov vs Oct.

text.p: Switzerland's Centre for Research of Economic Activity (KOF) said its economic barometer rose by 0.1 percent in November versus October.
Compared with November 1995, the barometer rose 0.8 percent.
KOF, part of the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich (ETH), also expected no real improvement in the Swiss economy in the first few months of 1997.
"Based on the development of the barometer in the second half of the past year, an improvement in the first months of this year is not expected," KOF said.
On a seasonally-adjusted basis, the barometer remained "clearly below the long-term average," it said.
KOF said leading indicators showed little or no improvement.
Outstanding orders in the machinery industry showed no gains in November, while construction continued to show declines. Employment indicators also continued to worsen.
The only gains were seen in the leading indicator "real monetary aggregate," it said.
Measured against the same 1995 month, the October barometer showed a revised increase of 0.7 percent, and the September barometer a revised increase of 0.5 percent.
It earlier had reported October up 0.9 percent and September up 1.1 percent versus a year ago.
